title: Your Neighbors Know: Leveraging Local Neighborhoods for Backdoor Detection in Decentralized Learning
abstract: arXiv:2605.19969v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Decentralized learning (DL) is an emerging machine learning paradigm where nodes collaboratively train models without a central server. However, the collaborative nature of DL makes it vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where a model is taught to behave normally on standard inputs while executing hidden, malicious actions when encountering data with specific triggers. Backdoor attacks in DL remain understudied and existing defenses often overlook DL constraints. We introduce Argus, a novel backdoor detection framework native to DL that requires neither a central coordinator nor prior knowledge of the trigger. In Argus, honest nodes locally analyze received model updates to identify potential backdoor triggers. Nodes then collectively share their triggers with their neighbors and use a structural similarity metric to separate true backdoors from false alarms induced by data heterogeneity. translated_abstract: 去中心化学习是一种新兴的机器学习范式，其中节点在没有中央服务器的情况下协作训练模型。然而，去中心化学习的协作特性使其容易受到后门攻击，即模型被训练为在标准输入上表现正常，而在遇到带有特定触发器的数据时执行隐藏的恶意操作。去中心化学习中的后门攻击目前仍研究不足，且现有防御方法往往忽视去中心化学习的约束条件。我们提出了Argus，一种原生支持去中心化学习的全新后门检测框架，它既不需要中央协调者，也不需要预先了解触发器。在Argus中，诚实节点在本地分析接收到的模型更新，以识别潜在的后门触发器。随后，节点将各自的触发器与邻居共享，并使用结构相似性度量来区分真正的后门与由数据异质性引起的误报。一个关键洞察是，误报的触发器（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了去中心化学习原生的新型后门检测框架Argus，无需中央协调者或触发器先验知识，通过节点本地分析模型更新、与邻居共享触发器并利用结构相似性度量，有效区分真实后门攻击与数据异质性导致的误报。
en_tdlr: Argus is a novel backdoor detection framework native to decentralized learning that requires neither a central coordinator nor prior knowledge of the trigger, where honest nodes locally analyze model updates, share detected triggers with neighbors, and use a structural similarity metric to separate true backdoors from false alarms induced by data heterogeneity.
